_comment: Narrative fact-check repairs. Each entry replaces `find` with `replace` in team_history.json[teamId][field] (or sets the field for kind=value). Only entries with status=approved are applied by scripts/apply_narrative_repairs.py. Findings source: FACTCHECK_FINDINGS_2026-06-11.md / FACTCHECK_FINDINGS_FULL_2026-06-12.md.

batch1.find: Before Wooden arrived in 1948, UCLA had never won a conference title
batch1.replace: Before Wooden arrived in 1948, UCLA had not won a conference title since 1927

batch1.find: once lost 39 straight games to rival USC
batch1.replace: once lost 42 straight games to rival USC between 1932 and 1943

batch1.find: Kentucky has led the nation in home attendance since 1976 and won the national attendance title a record 25 times
batch1.replace: Kentucky has won the national attendance title 29 times since Rupp Arena opened in 1976, more than any other program

batch1.find: Kansas's coaching lineage is unmatched: Naismith coached Allen, who coached Dean Smith and Adolph Rupp — between them, they won over 3,000 games and multiple national titles
batch1.replace: Kansas's coaching lineage is unmatched: Naismith coached Allen, who coached Dean Smith and Adolph Rupp — between them, they won more than 2,500 games and multiple national titles

batch1.find: The term 'Hoosier' has been associated with Indiana residents since the 1840s, though its exact origin remains debated among historians
batch1.replace: The term 'Hoosier' has been associated with Indiana residents since the early 1830s, though its exact origin remains debated among historians

batch1.find: The 'Wildcats' nickname has been used since the early days of the program, though the exact reason for its selection is lost to history
batch1.replace: The 'Wildcats' nickname was adopted in 1926 through a campus-wide contest, the winning suggestion of assistant football coach Edward Hunsinger, who had played at Notre Dame alongside the famed 'Four Horsemen'

batch1.find: ranks fifth all-time in total wins among NCAA programs
batch1.replace: ranks among the top ten NCAA programs in all-time wins

batch1.find: Syracuse has led the nation in attendance 25 times
batch1.replace: Syracuse has led the nation in attendance 16 times, including 11 straight seasons from 1985 to 1995

batch1.find: Houston won its first NCAA Championship in 2025, finally breaking through after heartbreaking losses in the 1980s.
batch1.replace: Houston is still chasing its first NCAA Championship, having reached seven Final Fours and lost national title games in 1983, 1984, and 2025 — the last a 65-63 heartbreaker against Florida.

batch1.find: Under Tom Izzo, who arrived in 1995, Michigan State has reached ten Final Fours and won a second national title in 2000.
batch1.replace: Under Tom Izzo, who arrived in 1995, Michigan State has reached eight Final Fours — ten in program history — and won a second national title in 2000.

batch1.find: Tom Izzo has led Michigan State to ten Final Fours, tied for sixth most all-time, and ESPN named the Spartans the best team of the 2000s decade
batch1.replace: Tom Izzo has led Michigan State to eight Final Fours, the fifth most by any coach all-time, and ESPN's Andy Katz picked the Spartans as his team of the 2000s decade

batch1.find: Under Ed Jucker, Cincinnati won back-to-back NCAA Championships in 1961 and 1962, becoming the last team to win consecutive titles until Duke in 1991-92.
batch1.replace: Under Ed Jucker, Cincinnati won back-to-back NCAA Championships in 1961 and 1962, and came within an overtime loss to Loyola Chicago of a third straight title in 1963.

batch1.find: Winning back-to-back NCAA Championships in 1961 and 1962 under coach Ed Jucker, the last team to repeat until Duke thirty years later
batch1.replace: Winning back-to-back NCAA Championships in 1961 and 1962 under coach Ed Jucker, then reaching a third straight title game in 1963

batch1.find: Adopted in 1914 when cheerleader Norman 'Pat' Lyon combined 'bear' and 'cats' after a cartoon of a ferocious bear-cat hybrid appeared in the school newspaper
batch1.replace: Born on Halloween 1914, when cheerleader Norman 'Pat' Lyon punned on star fullback Teddy Baehr's name — 'They may be Wildcats, but we have a Baehr-cat on our side' — during a win over Kentucky; a student newspaper cartoon of a 'Cincinnati Bear Cat' days later cemented the name

batch1.find: When Gonzaga opened McCarthey Athletic Center in 2004, the Bulldogs won 100 consecutive home games there, the longest such streak in the NCAA at the time
batch1.replace: Gonzaga opened McCarthey Athletic Center in 2004 riding a 38-game home winning streak, and later won 75 straight there from 2018 to 2023 — more than five years without a home loss

batch1.find: Kansas State has a proud basketball history, reaching the Final Four four times and finishing as national runner-up twice (1951, 1958).
batch1.replace: Kansas State has a proud basketball history, reaching the Final Four four times (1948, 1951, 1958, 1964) and finishing as national runner-up in 1951.

batch1.find: Despite being ranked No. 1 and undefeated, the 1943 'Whiz Kids' team opted not to play in the NCAA Tournament when three of its five starters were called to duty in World War II
batch1.replace: Despite a 17-1 record and recognition as the nation's best team, the 1943 'Whiz Kids' opted not to play in the NCAA Tournament when three of their five starters were called to duty in World War II

batch1.find: demolcing previously undefeated Gonzaga 86-70 in the title game
batch1.replace: demolishing previously undefeated Gonzaga 86-70 in the title game

batch1.find: inspired by a line from Oliver Goldsmith's poem 'The Deserted Village' referencing a 'bold peasantry.'
batch1.replace: inspired by the line 'where crouching tigers wait their hapless prey' from Oliver Goldsmith's poem 'The Deserted Village.'

batch1.find: Reaching the 2019 Final Four under Bruce Pearl, the program's first Final Four appearance in over 30 years, energizing the fan base
batch1.replace: Reaching the 2019 Final Four under Bruce Pearl, the first Final Four appearance in program history, capped by an overtime Elite Eight upset of Kentucky

batch1.find: Colorado State's Moby Arena, opened in 1966, was nicknamed 'Moby' both for its whale-like shape and as a pun on the arena's original name
batch1.replace: Colorado State's Moby Arena, dedicated in 1966, earned its nickname when a student sportswriter compared the hump-shaped building to the whale from Moby-Dick — 'Moby Gym' stuck, and the name was made official decades later

batch1.find: The program has made multiple NCAA Tournament appearances and reached the Sweet Sixteen.
batch1.replace: The program has made multiple NCAA Tournament appearances and earned its first tournament win in 2016 over California.

batch1.find: including two NCAA Tournament title claims in 1919 and 1937 (pre-tournament era)
batch1.replace: including retroactively awarded national championships for 1902 and 1919 from the Helms Athletic Foundation and 1903 from the Premo-Porretta Power Poll

batch1.find: The 2006 America East Tournament Championship and NCAA Tournament appearance, the program's first Big Dance bid in over a decade.
batch1.replace: Back-to-back 20-win seasons in 2015-16 and 2016-17 under Bill Herrion, the best stretch of the program's Division I era.

batch2.find: UNH's Lundholm Gymnasium was one of the most intimate and oldest venues in Division I basketball before the school moved to the larger Whittemore Center Arena.
batch2.replace: UNH's Lundholm Gymnasium, an intimate ~3,000-seat venue that opened in the 1930s, remains one of the oldest and smallest arenas in Division I basketball and is still the Wildcats' home court.

batch2.find: Upsetting No. 2 seed Syracuse 73-69 in the 2011 NCAA Tournament as a 12-seed, part of a run to the Sweet Sixteen under coach Chris Mooney.
batch2.replace: Upsetting No. 2 seed Syracuse 73-69 in the 1991 NCAA Tournament as a 15-seed, becoming the first 15-seed in tournament history to beat a 2-seed under coach Dick Tarrant.

batch2.find: Richmond is one of the few schools to have upset a No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3 seed in the NCAA Tournament across its history, earning a reputation as a giant-killer.
batch2.replace: Richmond is the only school to have won NCAA Tournament games as a No. 12, No. 13, No. 14, and No. 15 seed, earning a reputation as a giant-killer.

batch2.find: The 2004-05 season, when Pacific went 27-3 and earned a #6 seed in the NCAA Tournament, the program's highest seed and one of its best seasons in history.
batch2.replace: The 2004-05 season, when Pacific went 27-4 and a perfect 18-0 in the Big West, earned a #8 seed in the NCAA Tournament, beat No. 9 seed Pittsburgh, and fell to No. 1 seed Washington in the second round, one of the best seasons in program history.

batch2.find: The Tigers mascot was adopted in 1923, chosen for the animal's strength and ferocity, giving the Stockton-based university a powerful athletic identity.
batch2.replace: The Tigers nickname originated in the fall of 1908, when the rugby team's black jerseys and socks with orange stripes made the players look like tigers, and was made official by the 1925 student constitution.

batch2.find: The 'Blue Demons' name combines the school's signature blue color with an energetic and fierce spirit; the mascot is named DIBS (DePaul Intercollegiate Blue Spirit)
batch2.replace: The 'Blue Demons' name evolved from 'D-men' — early DePaul athletes wore a large 'D' on their sweaters, prompting fans to call them 'D-men,' which was formalized into 'Demons' in the 1920s; 'Blue' came from the university's designated color (the affiliated DePaul Academy took scarlet). The mascot is named DIBS (DePaul Intercollegiate Blue Spirit).

batch2.find: Georgia State's home arena was formerly Philips Arena (now State Farm Arena), the same venue used by the Atlanta Hawks — one of the few mid-major programs to share a venue with an NBA team.
batch2.replace: Georgia State men's basketball called the on-campus GSU Sports Arena home for nearly 50 years (1973-2022) before moving into the new 7,300-seat Georgia State Convocation Center near the former Turner Field for the 2022-23 season.

batch2.find: Mercyhurst University in Erie, Pennsylvania, began competing in Division I in 2023-24 as a member of the Northeast Conference.
batch2.replace: Mercyhurst University in Erie, Pennsylvania, began competing in Division I in 2024-25 as a member of the Northeast Conference.

batch2.find: The 2023 announcement of the transition to Division I, signaling a new era for Mercyhurst athletics and its basketball program.
batch2.replace: The 2024 announcement of the transition to Division I, signaling a new era for Mercyhurst athletics and its basketball program.

batch2.find: Radford's basketball program dates to 1920, and the Virginia school competes in the Big South Conference.
batch2.replace: Radford's men's basketball program dates to 1974, and the Virginia school is a charter member of the Big South Conference.

batch2.find: The 'Pirates' nickname was adopted in the 1930s, reflecting New Jersey's coastal heritage and seafaring history
batch2.replace: The 'Pirates' nickname was born on April 24, 1931, when a Newark News sportswriter, watching Seton Hall's baseball team steal a come-from-behind win over Holy Cross, called them 'a gang of Pirates' — a name that stuck.

batch2.find: The 'Pirates' nickname was chosen in the 1930s to reflect the school's New Jersey coastal heritage.
batch2.replace: The 'Pirates' nickname dates to 1931, when a sportswriter dubbed Seton Hall's comeback-minded baseball team 'a gang of Pirates.'

batch2.find: Making the 2004 Summit League tournament and competing for an NCAA Tournament berth, one of the program's most competitive recent eras.
batch2.replace: Going 22-9 in 2012-13 under coach Jim Molinari to share the Summit League regular-season title and earn a College Basketball Invitational bid, the winningest Division I season in program history.

batch2.find: The Dragons nickname was adopted in the early 1900s, with the mythical dragon representing power and the fiery spirit of the university's competitive teams.
batch2.replace: The Dragons nickname was adopted in 1928, announced in Drexel's student newspaper The Triangle, replacing 'The Engineers' so that athletes from all of the school's colleges — not just engineering — would be represented under a single fierce identity.

batch2.find: The Trailblazers name was adopted in 2022 as part of the school's rebranding from Dixie State to Utah Tech, symbolizing pioneering innovation and the spirit of the American West.
batch2.replace: The Trailblazers name was unveiled on April 11, 2016, replacing 'Red Storm' while the school was still Dixie State; the university later rebranded from Dixie State to Utah Tech, effective July 2022. The name symbolizes pioneering innovation and the spirit of the American West.

batch2.find: Upsetting No. 1 seed Iowa State in the 2015 NCAA Tournament as a 14-seed, capped by a Robert Brown three-pointer, just weeks after the university had threatened to shut down the program.
batch2.replace: Upsetting No. 3 seed Iowa State 60-59 in the 2015 NCAA Tournament as a 14-seed — Robert Brown scored 21 and hit a go-ahead three before William Lee's late basket and free throws sealed it — just months after the university had controversially shut down its football program.

batch2.find: The Blazers name was chosen in a student contest in 1978, referencing Birmingham's history as an iron and steel city — the city's blast furnaces "blazed" through the night.
batch2.replace: The Blazers name originated in late 1977 when history student Tommy Burns suggested 'Trail Blazers' — the new program blazing a trail for the school, partly inspired by the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers — which was shortened to 'Blazers' and won a January 1978 campus vote.

batch2.find: Chauncey Billups' stellar 1996-97 season, averaging 17.1 points as a sophomore before becoming the No. 3 overall NBA pick and eventual NBA Finals MVP.
batch2.replace: Chauncey Billups' stellar 1996-97 season, averaging 19.1 points as a sophomore before becoming the No. 3 overall NBA pick and eventual NBA Finals MVP.

batch2.find: As a founding member of the Missouri Valley Conference, SLU has a proud tradition in the Atlantic 10.
batch2.replace: A longtime member of the Missouri Valley Conference from 1937 to 1974, SLU carries that proud tradition into the Atlantic 10.

batch2.find: dates to 1914
batch2.replace: dates to 1912

batch2.find: began in 1957
batch2.replace: began in 1949

batch2.find: dates to around 1900, making it one of the oldest in the Midwest
batch2.replace: dates to 1915
batch2.note: companion to #70 founded fix; 'oldest in the Midwest' superlative dropped since it rested on the wrong 1900 date
